questions.q: Which call gives the value from the same weekday last week in a daily series?
why: Correct. shift(7) moves the series 7 steps later.
That is the value 7 days in the future.
diff(1) is the change from yesterday.

questions.q: y = [3, 5, 9, 15]. What is y.diff() at the last row?
A price falls from 80 to 60. What is the simple return?
A price rises by 10% and then falls by 10%. The start price is 100. What is the end price?
questions.why: 100 × 1.10 = 110, and 110 × 0.90 = 99. Simple returns do not cancel.

questions.q: Daily log returns are 0.01, 0.02, -0.005 and 0.015. The price at the start is 200. About what is the price at the end? (Use exp(0.04) = 1.0408.)
questions.why: The log returns add up to 0.04. The end price is 200 × exp(0.04) = 200 × 1.0408 = 208.16.

questions.q: Why do we prefer log returns when we combine many days?
why: Correct. The sum of daily log returns is the log return of the whole period.
They do not remove noise. They only change the scale.

questions.q: You build the feature 'sales yesterday' for each day with data that has missing rows. What should you do first?
options: Reindex to a full daily grid, then shift(1)
why: Correct. Then one row back is exactly one day back.
With missing rows, shift(1) can reach back more than one day.
shift(-1) is tomorrow, which is leakage.
